subject: Furniture around fireplaces and alcoves
hook: TV above the fireplace? Plan the cables before the cupboards.
ig:
TV above the fireplace? Plan the cables before the cupboards. Here's the order that keeps everything hidden.

The usual problem with a TV on the chimney breast: you end up with a cable dangling down the middle of it and a router balanced on the hearth.

The fix is sequence. Agree the TV height and size first. Then decide which alcove becomes the 'tech side' — that cupboard gets cable entry points, ventilation and space for a router and box. Only then do we design the shelves and doors around it.

Swipe for a typical project from survey to finish. Your electrician or aerial installer may need to move a socket or point before we fit, so it's worth knowing early.

Planning a TV between alcoves? Link in bio for our media walls page.
fb:
TV on the chimney breast, alcove units either side — it's one of the most requested living-room layouts we see, especially in older homes around Stoke-on-Trent.

The bit people don't think about until it's too late is the cables. This carousel walks through a typical project in the right order: TV position first, then the cable route, then the cupboards built around it. One alcove usually becomes the tech side, with ventilation for the router and box.

If you're weighing up a media wall or alcove units, our media walls page has more.

alt: Six frames: an alcove being measured, a survey sketch, a 3D render on a monitor, cut panels, a scribed filler and a floating console with hidden cables (AI concept images).
on_asset: F1: Survey — Measure both alcoves, the chimney breast and the hearth. Note the aerial point, sockets and whether the fire is in use. | F2: Decide the TV position — Mounting height and screen size are agreed first, because they set where every cable has to travel. | F3: Plan the cable route — A typical layout drops cables from the TV into one alcove, where the router and box live in a ventilated cupboard. | F4: Design in 3D — You see both alcove units with the TV in place and adjust shelf heights before anything is cut. | F5: Make and fit — Units cut, edged and assembled in our Hanley workshop, then installed and scribed to the walls. | F6: Done — Cables out of sight, kit behind doors, chimney breast left clear. Concept images throughout.
